thread.title: Mid-Day ETF Update: ETFs, Stocks Mixed on Disappointing Morgan Stanley Results, Renewed US-China Tensions

author: MT Newswires
title: Mid-Day ETF Update: ETFs, Stocks Mixed on Disappointing Morgan Stanley Results, Renewed US-China Tensions
text:
Shutterstock photo Active broad-market exchange-traded funds in Thursday's regular session:
iShares MSCI Emerging Index Fund ( EEM ): -0.2%
SPDR S&P 500 ( SPY ): +0.3%
SPDR Select Sector Fund - Financial ( XLF ): -0.2%
United States Oil Fund ( USO ): -0.8%
ProShares UltraPro Short QQQ ( SQQQ ): -0.5%
Broad Market Indicators
Broad-market exchange-traded funds, including IWM and IVV were higher. Actively traded PowerShares QQQ (QQQ) was up 0.2%.
US stocks were mixed at session's half, as investors comb through mixed quarterly results, the fallout from an extended government shutdown, and heightened tensions between the US and China after the US government opened an investigation into Huawei for stealing trade secrets.
In economic data news, business conditions in the mid-Atlantic region improved measurably in January as the Philadelphia Fed index jumped to 17.0 from 9.1 in December, well above estimates for an increase to 10.0.
Meanwhile, weekly jobless claims declined by 3,000 to 213,000 versus consensus of 221,000. Unemployment claims have declined to the lowest level since early December. Continuing claims fell by 1,000 to 220,750.
Power Play: Financial
The Select Financial Sector SPDRs ( XLF ) was up 0.2%. Direxion Daily Financial Bull 3X shares (FAS) was up 0.8% and its bearish counterpart Direxion Daily Financial Bear 3X shares (FAZ) was down 0.9%.
M&T Bank (MTB) was up 4% after the company posted Q4 earnings and revenue that topped analysts' expectations. The parent company of M&T Bank said adjusted earnings were $3.79 per share compared with $2.04 per share a year ago. Analysts polled by Capital IQ were expecting $3.49 per share. Revenue, calculated as the sum of net interest income and non-interest income, was $1.54 billion, up from $1.46 billion in the same quarter last year. The Street view was for revenue of $1.49 billion.
Winners and Losers
Technology
Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) was up 0.1%, while tech funds iShares Dow Jones US Technology ETF (IYW) and iShares S&P North American Technology ETF (IGM) were in the green.
Among semiconductor ETFs, SPDR S&P Semiconductor (XSD) was down 0.04% and Semiconductor Sector Index Fund (SOXX) was up 0.1%.
Apple (AAPL) was down 0.1% after DigiTimes, citing unidentified industry sources, reported that the company is planning to start selling two new iPad tablets in the first half of this year. General Interface Solution and TPK Holding, touch panel manufacturers based in Taiwan, will be supplying components for the devices, according to the report.
Industrial
Select Sector SPDR-Industrial (XLI) was up 0.6% and other funds iShares Trust Dow Jones U.S. Industrial Sector Index Fund (IYJ) and Vanguard Industrials (VIS) were higher.
Fastenal Company (FAST) rose more than 4% after it posted Q4 earnings of $0.59 per share, up from $0.53 in the same period a year ago but below the estimate of $0.60 from analysts polled by Capital IQ. Total revenue of $1.23 billion was up from $1.09 billion a year ago, exceeding the Street projection of $1.22 billion.
Energy
Dow Jones US Energy Fund (IYE) was up 0.2% and Energy Select Sector SPDR (XLE) was up 0.3%.
General Electric's (GE) GE Renewable Energy and Future Wind, a joint venture between Pondera Development and SIF Holding Netherlands, said Wednesday that they have agreed to install the first Haliade-X 12 MW wind turbine prototype in Maasvlakte-Rotterdam in the Netherlands this summer. The agreement includes five years of testing and a 15-year full-service operation and maintenance agreement. The Haliade-X prototype will be installed onshore for access during testing, according to a statement. During the initial period of operations, GE Renewable Energy will collect data required to secure a "Type Certificate," which is a key step in commercializing the product by 2021, according to the statement. GE shares were up 1.5%.
Commodities
Crude was down 0.3%. United States Oil Fund ( USO ) was down 0.7%. Natural gas up 0.9% while United States Natural Gas Fund (UNG) was up 0.9%.
Gold was up 0.5%. SPDR Gold Trust (GLD) was up 0.4%. Silver was up 0.1%, while iShares Silver Trust (SLV) was up 0.2%.
Consumer
Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR (XLP) was down 0.8% while Vanguard Consumer Staples ETF (VDC) and iShares Dow Jones U.S. Consumer Goods (IYK) were higher.
Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR (XLY) was up 0.1% while retail funds SPDR S&P Retail (XRT) and Market Vectors Retail ETF (RTH) were firmer.
Bassett Furniture Industries (BSET) fell nearly 12% after the retailer of home furnishings reported fiscal Q4 net income of $0.18 per share, down from $0.46 per share in the prior-year period. Two analysts polled by Capital IQ had been expecting $0.37 per share. Revenue for the quarter ended Nov. 24 was $116.7 million, down from $118.2 million reported for the same period last year. Two analysts polled by Capital IQ had been expecting revenue of $118.7 million.
Health Care
Health Care SPDR (XLV) was up 0.6%, and other health care funds including Vanguard Health Care ETF (VHT) and iShares Dow Jones U.S. Healthcare (IYH) were higher. Biotechnology fund iShares NASDAQ Biotechnology Index (IBB) was up 1%.
Lipocine (LPCN) rose nearly 25% after it said that interim results from a fat imaging study showed its drug LPCN 1144 achieved a "meaningful liver fat reduction" in patients with non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH). NASH is an advanced form of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) and occurs when fat accumulates in liver cells due to causes other than excessive alcohol use and a patient has hepatitis and liver cell damage. Currently there are no approved treatments for NASH. Based on multiple clinical studies with up to 52-week exposure, LPCN 1144 is well tolerated with no adverse liver enzyme signals.
